newsitem.title: FINLAND: EMU 3rd stage seen more likely to start than fail.
newsitem.headline: EMU 3rd stage seen more likely to start than fail.

text.p: The third stage of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) is more likely to start as planned than to fail, according to a Reuters Finnish Business News poll.
Most of the 22 respondents also expected Finland to be among the first countries to join the single-currency if the third stage started.
Forecasts for the likelihood of the third stage of EMU to come about ranged from 20 to 100 percent, with the mean at 69 percent. Nobody expected the project to fail completely.
The lowest probability came from a bank while a corporate treasury department topped the optimistic side, seeing absolutely no scope for a failure of the third stage to start.
Fourteen of the 22 dealers, analysts and economists at banks and corporate treasury departments expected the third phase of EMU to start on time.
One large bank saw a delay of four years while the other seven respondents expecting a belated start put kick-off between six months and 18 months after January 1999.
Twelve of 22 respondents said the probability that Finland will join EMU in the first wave was 75 percent or higher.
Four said it was 100-percent certain Finland will enter the third stage, while one saw no possibility for Finland to be in the first group.
One put the likelihod at 20 percent, and the rest estimated the probability between 50-75 percent.

The poll was done on Mondy and Tuesday with anonymous forecasts from Aktia Bank, Bank of America (London), Banque Indosuez (Stockholm), CD Derivatives Ltd, Davy Protos, Den Danske Bank (Copenhagen), Enskilda Banken Helsinki, Enso, Handelsbanken Markets Finland, Huhtamaki Finance, Interbank, IVO, Kemira, Kesko, Merita Bank, Neste, Nokia, OKOBANK, Postipankki, SOK, Unibank (Copenhagen) and UPM-Kymmene.
